text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing; please know that while I cannot hear your voice, I will rely on your caregivers to answer on your behalf to determine the cause. To start, do these breathing difficulties occur specifically when you are feeding or crying?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That information is very helpful. Given the vomiting after feeding and the worsening of symptoms with neck flexion, I need to confirm if there is a history of cyanosis or "tet spells" when the child is agitated. Did you notice any bluish discoloration around the lips or fingertips during these episodes?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Laryngoscopy: No intrinsic laryngeal masses, vocal cord paralysis, or subglottic stenosis observed; airway patency maintained despite stridor. Neck_Ultrasound: Sonographic evidence of vascular rings encircling the trachea and esophagus, consistent with a double aortic arch.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Double Aortic Arch causing tracheal compression and stridor.

The ultrasound findings of a vascular ring encircling both the trachea and esophagus, combined with symptoms worsening during feeding and neck flexion, are pathognomonic for this congenital anomaly. No further tests are required to confirm this diagnosis.
